deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls Terraform's own lifecycle management (destroy/abandon behaviour) rather than a platform-level security setting on the resource itself.

description.description:
An optional description of this resource. Provide this property when you
create the resource.
description.rationale: A free-text label with no functional effect on access, exposure, or data protection.

healthy_percent_threshold.description:
Can only be set if the 'policyType' field is
'BACKEND_SERVICE_POLICY'. Specifies the threshold (as a
percentage) of healthy endpoints required in order to consider the
aggregated health result HEALTHY. Defaults to '60'. Must be in
range [0, 100]. Not applicable if the 'policyType' field is
'DNB_PUBLIC_IP_POLICY'. Can be mutated. This field is optional,
and will be set to the default if unspecified. Note that both this
threshold and 'minHealthyThreshold' must be satisfied in order
for HEALTHY to be the aggregated result. "Endpoints" refers to network
endpoints within a Network Endpoint Group or instances within an Instance
Group.
healthy_percent_threshold.rationale: Tunes health-check sensitivity for availability/reliability purposes; it does not affect confidentiality, access control, or exposure.

min_healthy_threshold.description:
Can only be set if the 'policyType' field is
'BACKEND_SERVICE_POLICY'. Specifies the minimum number of
healthy endpoints required in order to consider the aggregated health
result HEALTHY. Defaults to '1'. Must be positive. Not
applicable if the 'policyType' field is
'DNB_PUBLIC_IP_POLICY'. Can be mutated. This field is optional,
and will be set to the default if unspecified. Note that both this
threshold and 'healthyPercentThreshold' must be satisfied in
order for HEALTHY to be the aggregated result. "Endpoints" refers to
network endpoints within a Network Endpoint Group or instances within an
Instance Group.
min_healthy_threshold.rationale: Availability/reliability tuning, similar to healthy_percent_threshold; not a security control.

name.description:
Name of the resource. Provided by the client when the resource is created.
The name must be 1-63 characters long, and comply with RFC1035.
Specifically, the name must be 1-63 characters long and match the regular
expression '[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?' which means the first
character must be a lowercase letter, and all following characters must
be a dash, lowercase letter, or digit, except the last character, which
cannot be a dash.
name.rationale: An identifier for the resource; it does not itself change security behaviour.

policy_type.description:
Specifies the type of the healthAggregationPolicy. The only allowed value
for global resources is 'DNS_PUBLIC_IP_POLICY'. The only allowed
value for regional resources is 'BACKEND_SERVICE_POLICY'. Must
be specified when the healthAggregationPolicy is created, and cannot be
mutated. Default value: "BACKEND_SERVICE_POLICY" Possible values: ["DNS_PUBLIC_IP_POLICY", "BACKEND_SERVICE_POLICY"]
policy_type.rationale: Selects which target type (public DNS vs internal backend) the health policy monitors, but does not itself create or change exposure; the underlying resources' own settings govern their actual security posture.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: The project determines resource ownership/location, similar to other identifier fields; it is not itself a security control.

region.description: URL of the region where the health aggregation policy resides.
region.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).
